validated_work_order.confidence_rationale: Every claim in findings 1-7 was checked against the source on the default branch, and the two that mattered most were checked by running code rather than by reading it. A throwaway probe test rendered a ReportCard and clicked four different targets: a native <button> descendant, a plain <span>, a text <input>, and the click surface itself. All four reached goToReport (navigate call counts 1, 2, 3, 4 in that order), so finding 1's guard gap is real and finding 5's objection to the proposed guard is real too — a strict `e.target !== e.currentTarget` guard would have suppressed all three descendant clicks including the plain span, breaking every real click. A second probe confirmed emotion writes style rules as text nodes in this test environment (19 <style> tags, non-empty reads) and captured the body's actual injected rule, which contains exactly the three values finding 4 says are unpinned. The react-query claim in finding 3 was checked against @tanstack/query-core 5.101.2 source (queryObserver.js:310 defines isLoading as isPending && isFetching), confirming the comment is false. The QA defect was tested live in a browser and does not reproduce. Confidence is below 90 only because findings 2 and 3 change a shared hook's return type and the exact shape the implementer settles on is a judgement call, and because the paused-query behaviour choice in finding 3 has no test that distinguishes it today.
validated_work_order.understanding:
This ticket collects eight review findings and one QA finding left over from PR #26 (issue #22), filed after that PR merged. They are not one defect: they are the tail of one PR, and the issue body says so — "Check each one still reproduces before planning it. They were written against the PR as it stood, and a later round can have fixed one. Some may not hold up: say so and drop them rather than implementing something that was never wrong."

I checked each one against main. Seven hold. One does not.

The QA finding — /reports/spending spinning forever on the demo budget — does not reproduce. I ran the app, took the demo budget, and loaded /reports/spending and /reports/crossover both by direct URL and by following QA's exact steps. Both render their complete reports: Monthly Spending shows its Live toggle, compare dropdowns, mode toggle, legend, the Spent/Spent Average/Budgeted figures and a fully drawn cumulative graph; Crossover shows its date range, category and account sidebars and the projection chart. No page error, no console error, no failed request. The reason is visible in the code: the second commit of PR #26 added exactly the isFirstLoad override to useDashboardWidget.ts and useReport.ts, and an id-less route such as /reports/spending is the one case that override exists for (enabled: !!id && !!type is false, so the query never fetches and react-query would otherwise leave status 'pending' forever). QA tested the PR before that fix landed. Per the issue body's own instruction I am dropping it rather than planning a fix for a defect that is not on the default branch.

That drop also dissolves the split question. The remaining seven findings are the review follow-ups of one PR, spread over four files, and they no longer have to share a work order with an unrelated route defect.

Two findings contradict each other as written and cannot both be implemented. Finding 1 says the click path needs the same guard the keydown path has. Finding 5 says the guard finding 1 proposes would break every real click, and is right. I resolved it below; the important part is that the resolution is a judgement call I am making explicitly so the implementer does not have to guess, and implementing finding 1 literally would be a regression.

Findings 2 and 3 are latent, not live — no consumer reads status or isSuccess, so nothing is broken today — but both are cheap to make true and cheap to leave lying.
validated_work_order.root_cause: PR #26 fixed a React validateDOMNesting warning by replacing the card's <Button> wrapper with a View carrying role="button". That removed the HTML-validity error but left the card's event handling two different shapes: the keydown path gained an explicit 'this press belongs to a descendant control, not the card' guard, while onClick stayed a bare goToReport. The two paths drifted because only one of them was given a rule. Findings 2 and 3 are a separate, smaller root cause: the isFirstLoad override was added as a targeted fix for id-less routes and shipped as a spread over the whole react-query result, so the object callers receive carries the derived flag next to the react-query fields the derivation deliberately contradicts, justified by a comment that misstates what it is.
validated_work_order.approach:
Four files, all in packages/desktop-client/src.

The click guard is the one real design decision, so it comes first. Finding 1's proposed guard, `if (e.target !== e.currentTarget) return`, is wrong, and my probe is why: on a real card a user's click target is essentially never the wrapper — it is the body View, a span, or a recharts SVG node. Guarding on target identity would suppress every click that has ever worked. Finding 5 identifies this exactly. So the guard is asymmetric with the keydown guard by necessity, not by omission: the keydown guard can compare against currentTarget because a keydown only ever starts on a focusable element, whereas a click can start anywhere, so the click guard has to ask a different question — did this click land on something interactive?

Replace onClick={goToReport} with a handler that first resolves the event target to its nearest interactive ancestor and returns early when that ancestor is not the card surface itself. Selector: button, input, select, textarea, a[href], [contenteditable], [role="button"], [role="link"], [role="checkbox"], [role="tab"], [role="menuitem"], plus a check that the matched element is not event.currentTarget. That check is load-bearing and is why the card's own role="button" does not block its own clicks. Behaviour this produces: a native control inside a card does not navigate (finding 1's actual complaint, and it is now symmetric with the keydown path); a recharts node, a span, or the body View still navigates, because closest() finds nothing interactive in an SVG subtree; a component-library Button still behaves as it does today, because react-aria's press handling stops propagation before the card sees the event, so the guard is belt-and-braces there rather than a behaviour change.

Finding 7 is a comment edit on the block at ReportCard.tsx:113-117, which currently explains why the card is not a <Button> and stops there. Extend it to record the trade the review flagged: role="button" with tabIndex={0} around focusable descendants is itself the ARIA nested-interactive shape, the fix moved the problem from an HTML-validity error to a semantic one, and CalendarCard is the case that makes it visible. No test is required for a comment; it is verified by reading it in review.

For the test file, finding 5 is the load-bearing change and findings 4 and 6 combine into one edit of the style assertions. The positive click case currently fires on the surface, so it passes identically with or without a guard — move it to fire on screen.getByText('Balance Forecast'), a descendant. Add a native-control click case to CardWithNativeInnerControls, mirroring the keydown cases already there, asserting navigate was not called. Then rewrite the single style case into three over the card body rather than the surface: the surface genuinely has no background (I confirmed the surface's own rule is background-free), and the body's rule genuinely carries background-color:var(--color-tableBackground), box-shadow:0 2px 6px, and :hover box-shadow:0 4px 6px — so all three of finding 4's claims are assertable today. Finding 6's objection is that injectedCssFor returns '' under emotion's CSSOM mode, which makes a not.toMatch assertion vacuously true; I confirmed it does not return '' in this environment, but the failure mode is real and cheap to close, so each style assertion is preceded by an explicit non-empty check that names what went wrong. Keep injectedCssFor rather than deleting it: finding 6 offers deletion as an option, but finding 4 needs the cascade, and getComputedStyle cannot see a :hover state in jsdom, so the helper is the only way to make the hover claim falsifiable.

For the two hooks, apply the same change to both since they are twins. Finding 2: stop spreading. Return an explicit object — { data, error, isPending, isLoading, fetchStatus } — so status, isSuccess and isInitialLoading are no longer visible alongside a derived isPending that disagrees with them. I grepped all thirteen useDashboardWidget consumers and the single useReport consumer: every one destructures only data plus one of the two overridden flags, and nothing anywhere reads error, status, isSuccess, isRefetching or refetch off either hook. fetchStatus stays because both hook test files read it directly and it is the field the derivation is actually about. error stays because it is not one of the contradictory fields and dropping it would be an API reduction the ticket did not ask for.

Finding 3: keep the expression, fix the comment. The comment claims 'This is react-query's own isLoading definition'. queryObserver.js:310 defines it as isPending && isFetching, and isFetching is fetchStatus === 'fetching'; the hook computes isPending && fetchStatus !== 'idle'. They differ in exactly one case — a paused, uncached query — and I chose the reviewer's first option rather than its second on purpose. Narrowing the hook to isPending && query.isFetching would make a paused offline query fall out of the loading branch and render an empty report with no explanation, which is a worse outcome than a spinner for a query that is genuinely still trying and may resume. So the expression stands, the comment is corrected to say what it computes, and it states deliberately that a paused query counts as loading and why. The same three-line fix applies to useReport.ts, which carries the comment by copy.

The two hook test files each get one added case asserting the returned object no longer carries status or isSuccess, so a future spread reappears as a failing test rather than a comment nobody reads.

Keep the keydown guard at lines 124-138 exactly as it is; the comment on it already explains the repeat and preventDefault ordering and must not change. Add the finding-7 trade-off paragraph to the existing comment block at lines 113-117, recording that role="button" with tabIndex={0} around focusable descendants is itself the ARIA nested-interactive shape, that this change moved the defect from an HTML-validity error to a semantic one, and that CalendarCard is the case that makes it visible.

Rewrite the comment at lines 20-24: drop 'This is react-query's own isLoading definition', state that the expression is isPending && fetchStatus !== 'idle', state that react-query's own isLoading is isPending && isFetching (queryObserver.js:310), and state that a paused query is deliberately counted as loading because it is still trying and may resume.
files.why: Findings 2 and 3. The returned object is internally contradictory on an id-less route (isPending === false while status === 'pending' and isSuccess === false), and the comment justifying it misdescribes react-query's own semantics. The isPending && isFetching alternative was rejected because it would send a paused offline query out of the loading branch into an unexplained empty render.

The click surface's injected emotion rules are read non-empty and contain no background or background-color declaration.

The card body's injected emotion rules are read non-empty and carry the resting box-shadow 0 2px 6px rgba(0, 0, 0, .15).
The card body's :hover rule is read non-empty and carries box-shadow 0 4px 6px rgba(0, 0, 0, .15), the hover deepening.
Every style assertion is preceded by an explicit non-empty check, so an empty cascade fails the test loudly instead of passing a not.toMatch vacuously.
The object returned by useDashboardWidget does not carry status, isSuccess or isInitialLoading, so no caller can observe isPending === false alongside status === 'pending'.

The existing three cases - disabled by a missing id, first load resolving, and staying loaded through a background refetch - still pass against the narrowed return, confirming data, isPending, isLoading and fetchStatus all survive the change.
The object returned by useReport does not carry status, isSuccess or isInitialLoading, for the same reason as useDashboardWidget.

The existing three cases - bare /reports/custom with no id, first load resolving, and staying loaded through a background refetch - still pass against the narrowed return; the first already reads result.current.fetchStatus directly, which is why that field is kept on the narrowed type.

risks: The click-guard selector is the one judgement call with real blast radius. Too narrow and finding 1's complaint survives for whatever control type was not listed; too broad and ordinary card clicks stop navigating. The selector is written to cover every natively interactive element and every ARIA interactive role the widget bodies actually use, and the closest() !== currentTarget check is what keeps the card's own role="button" from blocking itself - that check must not be dropped.

Narrowing the hook return type is a compile-time API reduction on a shared hook. I grepped every consumer and none reads a dropped field, but the grep covers this repo at this commit only; anything reaching the hook dynamically would surface at typecheck, not at runtime.

Keeping 'paused' counted as loading is a deliberate choice with no test distinguishing it today. Nothing in the repo exercises an offline paused query, so if that behaviour is wrong it will not be caught by any case in tests[]. The comment records the decision so a later reader can revisit it deliberately rather than by accident.

The style assertions read emotion's injected text nodes. That is reliable in this vitest environment (I confirmed 19 style tags and non-empty reads) but is exactly the fragility finding 6 describes - it would go silent under emotion's CSSOM mode. The added non-empty checks convert that silent pass into a loud failure, which bounds the risk rather than removing it.

React Compiler is enabled for desktop-client, so the new onClick closure is auto-memoized; this is not a concern, but the guard adds a closest() call per click on the card surface and per bubbled descendant click, which is a trivial cost on a click path.
out_of_scope: The QA finding - /reports/spending (and /reports/crossover) never finishing loading on the demo budget. Tested live and it does not reproduce: both routes render their complete reports on main with no console error and no failed request, because PR #26's second commit added the isFirstLoad override these id-less routes depend on. QA filed it against the PR before that fix landed. Dropped per the issue body's own instruction to drop findings that do not hold up, not deferred.

Renaming PR #26 to carry the mandatory [AI] prefix (finding 8). It is a merged pull request, not a file change, and .github/** is a forbidden path in .sdlc/config.yml. This is a human action on GitHub, not work this ticket can carry.

Replacing role="button" with a semantically correct nested-interactive structure. Finding 7 asks only that the trade be recorded, and doing the actual a11y restructure would change the click target and accessible name that the e2e selectors depend on - a much larger change than this follow-up ticket.

Any behaviour change to the keydown path. Finding 3's second option (narrowing isFirstLoad to isPending && query.isFetching) was considered and rejected: it would push a paused offline query out of the loading branch into an unexplained empty render.

A release note in upcoming-release-notes/. No user-visible behaviour changes: the click-guard fix removes a latent path that is unreachable today (finding 1 says so explicitly), the hook change is a type-level narrowing with no runtime effect, and the rest are comments and test assertions. A note for this would ship on its own and say nothing.

alternatives_considered.approach: Implement finding 1 literally: add if (e.target !== e.currentTarget) return to onClick, exactly as proposed.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: A regression, and finding 5 says so. My probe measured four click targets all reaching goToReport: native button (1), plain span (2), text input (3), surface (4). A target-identity guard suppresses the first three - so a plain click on a chart label or a body span, which is what a user actually does, would stop opening the report. Finding 5's exact words: 'The guard A recommends would therefore leave this test green while breaking every real click.' That is precisely the state the retargeted positive case exists to prevent.

alternatives_considered.approach: Keep onClick unguarded and instead wrap every interactive control in a widget body with its own stopPropagation, the way react-aria's Button already does.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It pushes the burden onto every future widget body, and the bodies are third-party-ish render code (recharts, CalendarGraph) rather than code this change owns. ReportCard is the single place that knows the rule, so the rule belongs there - which is also what finding 1 asks for, minus the wrong predicate.

alternatives_considered.approach: Delete injectedCssFor and assert AC-5's claims some other way (finding 6 offers this).
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: getComputedStyle cannot resolve a :hover state in jsdom - a hover state does not exist there - so removing the helper makes the hover-deepening claim unassertable, which is one of the three claims finding 4 exists to pin. Keeping the helper with explicit non-empty guards takes finding 6's actual objection (silent emptiness) while preserving finding 4's requirement.

alternatives_considered.approach: For finding 2, keep the spread and instead derive status and isSuccess to agree with the overridden isPending.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It makes the object agree by asserting something false - status would be 'success' on a route that has never fetched. A narrowed type is the honest fix: it makes the contradiction unrepresentable rather than papering over it.

alternatives_considered.approach: For finding 3, narrow the expression to isPending && query.isFetching so the existing comment becomes true and the isLoading override is exactly redundant.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It changes behaviour in the one case the two expressions differ, and changes it for the worse. A paused query with no cached data (offline, first visit) would leave the loading branch and render an empty report with no explanation, where today it spins - a spinner for a query that is genuinely still trying is the better of the two. The reviewer's first option - say what the expression actually is and keep 'paused' deliberately - is correct here, so the comment is what changes.

alternatives_considered.approach: Split this ticket into a ReportCard work order and a hooks work order.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Premature, and the split question dissolved on its own. The two groups are independent in code but both are the review tail of one PR, together they touch four files, and the maintainer config clubs changes under six files. Splitting now would cost a second full plan-and-review round for no separation of risk. Noted in unknowns in case review prefers otherwise.

alternatives_considered.approach: Reopen the QA defect and plan a fix for the infinite spinner.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: There is no defect on main to fix. /reports/spending and /reports/crossover both render fully in the browser on the demo budget. Planning work against a bug that cannot be reproduced would produce a change with no failing case and no way to verify it - and the issue body explicitly warns against 'implementing something that was never wrong'.

assumptions: main is the branch QA's finding was measured against, and PR #26 is merged into it - the git log shows d11211f 'fix: Reports dashboard loads without React's nested-button warning' and 8efc33f 'Follow-ups from #42' on top of it, so the isFirstLoad fix is present.

The QA environment's demo budget data is equivalent to the one I loaded via 'Try the demo'. If QA's demo budget had zero transactions, a different symptom could have been at play - but both routes rendered real data and real charts in my run, which is the opposite of a data-starved failure.

Finding 1's claim that no such native control is reachable today is accepted rather than independently re-derived. It does not change the plan: the guard is correct regardless of whether any body currently renders one, and the test fixture CardWithNativeInnerControls already exists precisely to exercise it.

The 13 useDashboardWidget consumers and 1 useReport consumers enumerated by grep at this commit are the complete set - the hooks are only imported from packages/desktop-client, and grep for the import specifier found no other call sites.
Issue #22's AC-5 refers to the card-body styling claims as reproduced in finding 4's text; this ticket treats finding 4's prose as the specification of what to assert.
unknowns: Whether the paused-query loading behaviour should be tested. Nothing in the repo exercises it, so the choice made here (keep 'paused' as loading) is recorded in a comment rather than pinned by a case. If review wants it pinned, it needs a query client configured with networkMode: 'offlineFirst' or an equivalent, which I did not attempt.

Whether review would prefer findings 2-3 and 1/4/5/6/7 split into two tickets. I judged one work order correct on file count and shared origin; if the council disagrees, the split is clean because the two groups touch disjoint files.

Whether finding 6's underlying concern - emotion switching to CSSOM mode - can occur in this repo's vitest configuration at all. It does not at this commit; the non-empty guards make the question moot either way, but I did not trace why text mode is selected here.

Whether an interactive element type exists in a widget body that my selector does not cover. I covered every natively interactive element plus the ARIA interactive roles the bodies use; a custom widget body using a non-standard role could still need the selector widened. No such body is in the repo today.
evidence: The QA finding does not reproduce. I ran yarn start, took the demo budget via 'Try the demo', and loaded /reports/spending and /reports/crossover both by direct URL and by following QA's exact steps (Reports, then /reports/spending). Both render their complete reports - Monthly Spending with its Live toggle, compare dropdowns, mode toggle, legend, Spent/Spent Average/Budgeted figures and a drawn cumulative graph; Crossover with its Oct 2025 - Sep 2026 range, category and account sidebars and projection chart. No pageerror, no console errors, no failed requests.

Why it does not reproduce: PR #26's second commit added the isFirstLoad override to useDashboardWidget.ts:25 and useReport.ts:15, and an id-less route is exactly the case it exists for - enabled: !!id && !!type is false, so the query never fetches and react-query would otherwise leave status 'pending' forever, which Spending.tsx:64-66 and Crossover.tsx:65-67 render as <LoadingIndicator />. QA measured the PR before that commit.

Finding 1 verified live, not by reading. A throwaway probe test rendered a ReportCard with native controls in its body and clicked four targets in sequence. Navigate call counts came back 1, 2, 3, 4: the native <button> click navigated (1), the plain <span> click navigated (2), the text <input> click navigated (3), and the surface click navigated (4). Every descendant click reaches goToReport - the guard gap is real.

Finding 5 verified, and it is why finding 1 cannot be implemented as written. The same probe shows the plain-span click navigating, which a strict e.target !== e.currentTarget guard would suppress. A user clicks the body View, a span or a recharts SVG node, never the wrapper. The probe file was deleted; git status is clean apart from the untracked plan/ directory.

Finding 6's premise checked and found to be a latent risk rather than a live failure in this environment: injectedCssFor returned 453 characters for the click surface across 19 <style> tags, so emotion is writing text nodes under vitest, not the CSSOM. The silent-empty failure mode is still real under speedy mode, so the plan keeps the helper and adds explicit non-empty checks.

Finding 4 verified as assertable today. The card body's actual injected rule reads: background-color:var(--color-tableBackground); box-shadow:0 2px 6px rgba(0, 0, 0, .15); and, as a separate rule, .css-XXXX:hover{box-shadow:0 4px 6px rgba(0, 0, 0, .15)}.
